stories.title: What You Can Learn from a Competitor’s Job Postings
stories.description: Executives spend heavily trying to predict competitors’ next moves, yet often overlook one of the clearest signals of strategic intent: job postings. Because companies must hire before they can launch products, enter new markets, or build new capabilities, recruiting data often reveals future priorities months before earnings calls, press releases, or product announcements. By analyzing what capabilities competitors are building, where they are hiring, and how recruiting patterns change over time, managers can uncover emerging strategies and respond sooner. Hiring data is most powerful when combined with other intelligence sources and interpreted as patterns rather than isolated postings. Used well, it transforms public recruiting activity into a practical source of forward-looking competitive intelligence.

stories.title: Enhancing pan-cancer spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution with stPainter
stories.description: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics can resolve tissue architecture at cellular scale, but sparse gene panels and limited detection sensitivity constrain downstream analysis. Existing enhancement methods often require tissue-matched single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) references and dataset-specific retraining. Here we show that stPainter, a conditional generative model pretrained on a pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas, can enhance spatial transcriptomics data without matched references or retraining. Using a latent diffusion architecture guided by Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE), stPainter reconstructs expanded expression profiles from sparse measurements and produces latent representations for clustering and cell-state analysis. When we apply stPainter upon 6 spatial transcriptomics datasets of different cancer types, we demonstrate that our model empowers downstream biological analyses, including fine-grained subpopulation clustering and pathway enrichment. Comparison with spatially resolved proteomics (CODEX) provided independent support for regional agreement between imputed cellular compositions and protein-level tissue organization. These results establish stPainter as a scalable approach for analyzing tumor microenvironments without auxiliary sequencing data. This study presents stPainter, a pan-cancer pretrained model that enhances sparse spatial transcriptomics data and supports analysis of cellular organization across tumor tissues without matched single-cell references.

stories.title: The association between human development index and COVID-19 vaccination coverage
stories.description: The strategic deployment of COVID-19 vaccination is a cornerstone of the global pandemic response. However, equitable access to vaccines remains a critical challenge. This study was designed to investigate the association between COVID-19 vaccination coverage and the Human Development Index (HDI), and health system capacity at a global level. In this ecological study, data from 130 countries were analyzed. The dataset included the cumulative proportion of the COVID-19 fully vaccinated population, the HDI, its components (Life expectancy at birth, mean years of schooling, and Gross National Income (GNI) per capita), average routine vaccination coverage and universal health coverage (UHC), and World Bank income classifications. The associations between COVID-19 vaccination coverage, HDI, and its components were assessed using Spearman’s correlation coefficients and visualized with scatter plots Also, a multivariable linear regression model was done to control for confounders. A very strong positive correlation was observed between COVID-19 vaccination coverage and HDI (r = 0.86, p < 0.001). Strong positive correlations were also found with the components of HDI: life expectancy at birth (r = 0.84, p < 0.001), mean years of schooling (r = 0.74, p < 0.001), and Gross National Income per capita (r = 0.73, p < 0.001). When stratified by country income level, these correlations were most pronounced in lower-middle-income and upper-middle-income countries compared to low-income and high-income countries. In the multivariable model, HDI (β = 60.39, P = 0.003) and UHC (β = 0.91, P < 0.001) remained independent predictors, jointly explaining 76% of the between-country variation in COVID-19 vaccination coverage. HDI and UHC were strong independent predictors of COVID-19 vaccination coverage, indicating that equitable vaccine uptake depends on both socioeconomic development and health system capacity. Strengthening UHC, alongside long-term investments in education, health, and social development should be central to future pandemic preparedness and global vaccination strategies, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

stories.title: Evaluation of permeability damage in tight sandstone from hydroxypropyl guar fracturing fluids after prolonged exposure
stories.description: Hydraulic fracturing fluids used in tight gas wells may remain in the formation for extended periods before flowback because of operational and environmental constraints. This prolonged shut-in period can increase the potential for additional formation damage. This study evaluated the long-term impact, up to 6 months, of a hydroxypropyl guar-based (HPG) cross-linked fracturing fluid on the permeability of Scioto tight sandstone under high-temperature reservoir conditions. It represents one of the first systematic investigations of such extended fluid exposure durations. Core flooding experiments were conducted to determine the initial and regained permeability after thermal aging at 145 °C for 1, 3, and 6 months. FTIR, XRD, and TGA analyses were performed on the dried unbroken fluid, broken fluid, and recovered residue to characterize polymer degradation and the formation of inorganic solids. The core flooding results showed limited permeability impairment after the initial cleanup, reaching up to 11%. However, the results indicate a progressive decline in regained permeability with longer aging periods, with the loss becoming partly irreversible and reaching an additional 38% after 6 months under the tested conditions. SEM–EDX analysis showed that carbon and oxygen were the dominant elements in all samples, while boron was detected at every fluid stage and in the residue. XRD confirmed that the residue consisted mainly of boron-bearing solids (B₂O₃/HBO₂) together with amorphous polymeric material. Treatment of the residue with HCl at 145 °C for 40 h substantially reduced the amount of insoluble material, leaving mainly large coarse particles within two dominant size ranges, from several hundred to about 1,000 µm and around 2,000 µm, with only a minor fraction below 100 µm. Although these particles were much larger than the pore throats of tight sandstone, their size distribution in fractured formations may provide adequate coverage to mitigate damage associated with large residue clumps. Overall, the findings suggest that prolonged fluid contact promotes the accumulation of persistent inorganic residues that impair permeability, while high-temperature HCl treatment dissolves most of the residue mass, indicating a potential mitigation route whose effect on core permeability recovery remains to be verified.
